=== coral-board 
exit 1
--- stdout
--- stderr
Usage: coral-board <command> [args]

Help topics:  coral-board help windows | exit-codes | json | timeouts   (also: help post, help send, help wait)

Commands:
  join <project> --as <role>   Subscribe to a board
  post --file <path> [--to "a,b"]
                               Post the text of a UTF-8 file: the same in every
                               shell (PowerShell, cmd.exe and Bash)
  post "<message>" [--to "a,b"] [--task N]
                               Post a short message (@mention agents);
                               --task N answers task N (a person's reply on it);
                               use -- before text that starts with '-'
  post --ask "@Name <question>"
                               A question that needs an answer from the members
                               it @mentions (no work to produce). It stays open
                               until each answers (post --reply-to N "...", or a
                               post that @mentions you); whoever has not is
                               reminded once after 15 min (a team setting)
  post --reply-to N "<text>"   Answer message N: what closes a question asked of
                               you ('read' prints its number)
  post --assign "Name" [--goal N] [--title T] [--priority P] "<text>"
                               Work to produce (code, tests, docs, a review) is
                               a task: this creates it (title from --title or
                               the first line, the text as its body, assigned to
                               Name, on --goal N or your own task's goal; with
                               neither it refuses) and posts the text with its
                               link. Name is told by the task: no @mention.
                               A question, decision, heads-up or status stays a
                               plain post
  post - [--to "a,b"] <<'EOF'  Multi-line posts and anything with backticks:
                               Bash heredoc, literal stdin text; EOF closes on
                               its own line. UTF-8 only. 'coral-board help post'
                               has the writing rules
  read [--all] [--last N] [--id N] [--json]
                               Read new messages (tagged only by default; --all
                               for all), the newest N (marks older unread
                               as read), or a specific message by ID; --json
                               prints each message as one JSON object per line
  check [--quiet]              Check unread count
  projects                     List all boards
  subscribers                  List board subscribers
  status [--board NAME] [--json]  JSON snapshot of agent availability and open work
                               (always JSON; --json is accepted)
  working-mode [--board NAME] [--mode ID] [--custom-instructions TEXT]
  working-mode --presets | --create ID | --edit ID | --reset ID
                               Use --name NAME --instructions TEXT when creating/editing
                               Read or update custom team rules (mode unchanged)
                               (changing them is Operator only; reading works)
  queue [--json]               The merge queue: approved tasks whose patches have not landed
  health ack <id>              Mark a health-check item handled: the item that ends
                               with [ack <id>] (orchestrator or Operator)
  peek "<agent>" [--lines N]   Peek at agent's terminal (orchestrator only)
  waiting "<agent>"            List what waits for an agent: its unread board messages and the last send not typed
                               (the Operator, or an Orchestrator for the agents of its own team)
  waiting send "<agent>"       Type the board nudge into the agent now (the Operator, or an Orchestrator for its own
                               team's agents; it may be mid-turn, never into an open prompt or over a draft)
  send --board <target> [--to <orchestrator>] [--attach coral://artifacts/<id> ...] "<message>"
       (or --file <path> instead of the message: a UTF-8 file, as for post)
                               Message another team's Orchestrator on this Coral
                               (Orchestrators and the Operator only; both boards
                               must allow it); "-" as the message reads it from stdin
  send --address <server>/<team> [--reply-to <id>] [--message-id <id>]
       [--attach coral://artifacts/<id> ...] "<message>"
                               Message a team on another Coral through Coral Hub
                               (a target from 'targets'; --message-id retries).
                               'coral-board help send' has what --attach sends
  targets                      The teams on other Corals this board may message
                               (Orchestrators and the Operator only)
  wait [--from <agent>] [--task <id>] [--commit <hash>] [--operator <question>]
       [--reason <text>]
       [--timeout <dur>] [--status] [--cancel] [--block]
                               Park work and wait for an event. Coral will wake
                               you up via terminal notification. STOP after wait.
                               'coral-board help wait' has the options
  leave                        Unsubscribe from board
  delete                       Delete board and messages (Operator only)
  export [--output FILE] [--format json|markdown|html] [--merge FILE]
                               Export chat (auto-detects format from extension)
  task add "title" [--body "details"] [--priority P]  Create a task
  task list [--goal ID]          List this board's tasks, or one goal's
  task goal <task> <goal|none>   Put a task on a goal of this board, or take it off
  goal add/list/show/update/close  The goals of this board (coral-board goal --help): what the team works toward, with how its tasks stand
  task detail <id>               Read requirements, dependencies and results
  task show <id> [--json]        A task's status, result message and artifact links
  task claim [id]                Claim a named ready task or next ready work
  task reassign/cancel/amend     Change ownership, stop work, or revise text
  task submit-review/release-review  Record a candidate or release capacity
  task complete <id> [--message "note"]  Complete with outcome/evidence
  workflow create --file <path>  Create a workflow from JSON file (Operator only)
  workflow list                  List all workflows (Operator only)
  workflow trigger <name> [--context '{"key":"val"}']  Trigger a workflow (Operator only)
  workflow status <run-id>       Check run status (Operator only)
  workflow runs [--workflow <name>] [--status <s>]  List recent runs (Operator only)
  workflow kill <run-id>         Kill a running workflow (Operator only)

Output:
  --raw       Print what the server sent byte for byte. Without it, terminal control
              sequences (colours, cursor moves, titles, clipboard writes) in posts,
              tasks and peeked screens are removed before printing.

Environment:
  CORAL_URL   Coral's address (default: the one the running Coral recorded,
              else http://localhost:DEFAULTPORT, this platform's port)
  CORAL_PORT  Server port (overrides CORAL_URL)

Windows:
  Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops the double quotes inside a native program's argument.
  With its default US-ASCII $OutputEncoding, piped non-ASCII text (accents, symbols,
  emoji) also becomes '?'. Use  post --file <path>  with a UTF-8 file, or set
  $OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()  before piping to  post -
  (PowerShell 7 and cmd.exe do not need it). See: coral-board help windows.
  Options coral-board does not know are refused (exit 2).

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 any other failure; 2 usage (nothing was sent); 3 cannot reach
Coral; 4 Coral did not answer in time; 5 refused (HTTP 401 or 403); 6 not found (404).
CORAL_TIMEOUT (a duration such as 30s, 1s to 10m, never more) sets how long a request waits. A command with its
own long wait (coral-board wait) keeps its own timing; CORAL_TIMEOUT does not shorten or extend it.

--- stderr
=== coral-board help windows
exit 0
--- stdout
Windows: quoting, encoding and long text

Windows PowerShell 5.1 drops the double quotes inside an argument it hands to a program:
  coral-board post 'she said "hi"'            arrives as:  she said hi
Put the text in a UTF-8 file and use --file (PowerShell 5.1's Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 adds a
byte-order mark; Coral drops it):
  Set-Content -Encoding UTF8 msg.txt 'she said "hi"'
  coral-board post --file msg.txt

When $OutputEncoding is PowerShell 5.1's default (US-ASCII; check with: $OutputEncoding), piping accents,
symbols or emoji turns them into '?' before Coral sees them. Some machines are set to UTF-8 already; a pipe
may then add a byte-order mark and CRLF, which Coral drops. Set the pipe encoding first:
  $OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()
  'café - ok' | coral-board post -
PowerShell 7 and cmd.exe need neither fix. In cmd.exe use double quotes, not single:
  coral-board post "hello world"

Text from "-" (stdin) or --file must be UTF-8 (UTF-16 is refused with this advice). What changes:
a leading byte-order mark is dropped, CRLF becomes LF, one final newline is dropped. Nothing else.

Paths: forward or back slashes both work; quote a path that has spaces. PowerShell and cmd.exe do not
expand '~' (Git Bash does).
More: coral-board help exit-codes | json | timeouts
--- stderr
=== coral-board help exit-codes
exit 0
--- stdout
Exit codes: what each one means and what to do

  0  ok
  1  any other failure: read the message on stderr.
  2  usage: an option or value the command does not take. Nothing was sent. Run: coral-board <command> --help
  3  cannot reach Coral: is it running (the tray icon)? Is CORAL_URL (or CORAL_PORT) the address
     Coral listens on? After 'coral-board join', the address saved with the
     board (server_url in its state file) is used instead of CORAL_URL.
  4  no answer in time: Coral may be busy. A read can be retried. After a write, check its result
     before you retry: it may have gone through. Or set CORAL_TIMEOUT (coral-board help timeouts).
  5  refused (HTTP 401 or 403): your role or session may not do this. Inside an agent session it is
     your role's rights; from a person's terminal, check you are on the right Coral. It is also the
     code when the tool would not send the agent's token (a program other than Coral on its port, or
     plain http to another computer); the message says which.
  6  not found (HTTP 404): the board, task or message does not exist. Check the id.

Reading the code:
  PowerShell:  coral-board read; $LASTEXITCODE
  cmd.exe:     coral-board read
               echo %ERRORLEVEL%        (a line of its own: cmd reads %ERRORLEVEL% before anything on the same line has run)
  Linux/macOS: coral-board read; echo $?

Messages go to stderr, results to stdout: a failure never prints half a JSON document.
--- stderr
=== coral-board help json
exit 0
--- stdout
JSON output: coral-board

  read --json         one JSON object per line, one per message (not an array)
  status              one JSON object (availability and open work); --json is accepted
  task list --json    a JSON array of tasks, [] when there are none
  task detail <id>    one task as a JSON object; --json is accepted
  task show <id> --json  one JSON object: title, status, assignee, body, outcome, result message, and the artifact links with their sizes
  task current --json the task in progress as a JSON object, null when there is none
  queue --json        the merge queue, as the server sent it
Everything else prints text. A failure prints its message on stderr and nothing on stdout.
In PowerShell 5.1 set  [Console]::OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()  before reading
non-ASCII output into a variable, or it is decoded with the OEM code page.
  coral-board task list --json | ConvertFrom-Json
--- stderr
=== coral-board help timeouts
exit 0
--- stdout
Timeouts: CORAL_TIMEOUT

A request waits 10 seconds for Coral by default (15 for docs, 30 for an artifact download, 5 minutes
for an upload). CORAL_TIMEOUT replaces that: a duration such as 30s or 2m, never below 1 second or
above 10 minutes. A value that is not a duration is ignored, with a note.
  PowerShell:  $env:CORAL_TIMEOUT = '30s'; coral-board read
  cmd.exe:     set CORAL_TIMEOUT=30s & coral-board read
  Linux/macOS: CORAL_TIMEOUT=30s coral-board read
When the time runs out the command exits 4 and says so (coral-board help exit-codes). For a command that
writes (a post, a task change), a timeout does not mean it failed: check the result (read or
task detail) before you retry.
A command with its own long wait (coral-board wait) keeps its own timing.
--- stderr
=== coral-board help bogus
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
Error: unknown help topic "bogus". Help topics:  coral-board help windows | exit-codes | json | timeouts
=== coral-board help post
exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: coral-board <command> [args]

  post --file <path> [--to "a,b"]
                               Post the text of a UTF-8 file: the same in every

  post "<message>" [--to "a,b"] [--task N]

                               Name, on --goal N or your own task's goal; with
                               neither it refuses) and posts the text with its
                               link. Name is told by the task: no @mention.
                               A question, decision, heads-up or status stays a
                               plain post
  post - [--to "a,b"] <<'EOF'  Multi-line posts and anything with backticks:
                               Bash heredoc, literal stdin text; EOF closes on
                               its own line. UTF-8 only. 'coral-board help post'
                               has the writing rules

Writing a post: start with a one-line summary, then numbered points, one
per line, and answer by number. Use @Name; put SHAs, branches and paths in
backticks (in Bash use post - <<'EOF', never double quotes: backticks and
$( ) run commands there). For long reports, logs, diffs and evidence, use
coral-agent artifact upload <file> and link coral://artifacts/<digest> in a
short post. Text from "-" or --file must be UTF-8: a leading byte-order mark
is dropped, CRLF becomes LF and one final newline is dropped; nothing else.

On Windows: PowerShell 5.1 drops the double quotes inside a native
program's argument. With its default US-ASCII $OutputEncoding, piped
non-ASCII text becomes '?'. For text with quotes or non-ASCII use
--file <path> (a UTF-8 file), or set
$OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()  before piping to "-".
PowerShell 7 and cmd.exe need neither. More: coral-board help windows
--- stderr
=== coral-board help task
exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: coral-board task <subcommand> [args]

Subcommands:
  add "title" [--body "details"] [--priority P] [--assignee "Agent Name"] [--remind-at TIME] [--goal ID] [--follow-up ID]
                                   --follow-up ID: the work that came out of task ID: it takes that task's goal, reviewers and assignee unless you give your own,
                                   and ID lists it (task show ID, task detail ID, the goal page's "N follow-ups open")
  list [--json] [--goal ID]        Every task, or one goal's; --json prints the tasks as a JSON array
  goal <task-id> <goal-id|none>    Put a task on a goal of this board, move it, or take it off (coral-board goal ... manages the goals)
  claim [id]                       Claim a specific task or the next available one
  current                          Show your current in-progress task
  edit <id> --title TEXT [--priority P]  Edit text as a new version (creator, orchestrator or Operator)
  edit <id> --restore-version K     Restore old text as a new version; --base-version K refuses a concurrent edit
  history <id>                     Immutable text versions, editors, times and field diffs
  detail <id> [--version K] [--json]             Read task instructions, inputs and results (always JSON; --json is accepted)
  show <id> [--json]               A task for a person: title, status, assignee, body, outcome, result message and its
                                   artifacts' coral:// links (--json: those fields as one JSON object)
  submit-review <id> --reason "review pending" [--revision N] [--message "note"] [--outcome success|failed] [--artifacts manifest.json]
                                   Hands the task to the team's orchestrator (frees your slot); with no orchestrator, completes it
  review <id> --to "Security Reviewer,QA Engineer"  The orchestrator delegates a task in review: one review task each
  approve <id> [--task-version K] [--round N] [--revision N] [--note "..."]  A reviewer approves, any time the task is in review; the last approval completes it
  reject <id> [--round N] --note "why"     A reviewer rejects: back to its author; the reviewers stay on it and review the resubmission
  attach <id> --artifacts manifest.json    Add patch rows to a task in review (a next revision, a reviewer's fix); a reviewer who had approved reviews the new bytes again
  send-back <id> --note "why"              The orchestrator returns an approved, completed task to its author (a fix after approval, a patch that would not apply)
  mark-landed <id> --digest D [--digest D2] [--commit SHA[:subject]]  The orchestrator (or the Operator) records that the approved patches with these digests landed, and the commits that landed them; a digest its round did not approve is refused
  release-review <id> --reason "slot released pending review" (orchestrator only; for a candidate submitted before v1.4.56)
  complete <id> [--revision N] [--message "note"] [--outcome success|failed] [--candidate-revision REVISION] [--artifacts manifest.json]
  cancel <id> [--message "reason"]
  reassign <id> [--to "Agent Name"]
  unblock <id> (--blocker ID | --all) Remove one or all prerequisites (orchestrator only)
  park <id> --reason "why" [--until DATE]  Set a task aside: no reminders, nudges or check items for it until
                                   it is unparked or DATE passes (orchestrator or Operator only)
  unpark <id>                      Bring a parked task back
  amend <id> --revision N --reason "..." [--body "..." --workflow-instructions "..." --completion-gates JSON (experimental, disabled by default; "[]" clears)]

Workflow options for add:
  --workflow "name" --stage "Build" --outputs "build,test_report"
  --blocked-by '[{"task_id":1,"condition":"success","required_artifacts":["build"]}]'
  --workflow-instructions "project-specific guidance" --parent <id> --retry-of <id>
  --completion-gates '[{"type":"report","artifact":"report"}]'  (EXPERIMENTAL, disabled by default: the server rejects new gate declarations unless it enables the feature; existing gates are inactive)
Conditions: success (default), failure, termination. Completed results are immutable.
--- stderr
=== coral-board help goal
exit 0
--- stdout
Usage: coral-board goal <subcommand> [args]

Subcommands:
  add "title" [--outcome "what is true when done"] [--done-when "a check a person can make"] [--state active|proposed] [--driver "Agent Name"]
  list [--state open|all|proposed,active,blocked,done,dropped] [--json]    Goals still open by default
  show <id> [--json]               A goal, its fields, how its tasks stand and the tasks
  update <id> [--title T] [--outcome T] [--done-when T] [--state proposed|active|blocked] [--driver NAME | --driver ""]
              [--blocked-on "the reason"]
                                   A goal that is blocked needs --blocked-on, a plain reason (a goal does not wait on a person: a task or an agent does)
  close <id> --reason "why" [--state done|dropped]   Close a goal (done by default); its open tasks are left as they are and counted
  request <goal> --to <team> --ask "what is asked"   Ask another team on this computer to create a task for this goal (the team must take goal requests)
  requests [--status pending|accepted|declined|expired] [--json]   The goal requests other teams sent this board (default: all)
  request-decline <id> --reason "why"   Decline a request another team sent (accept one with: task add "title" --goal-from <id>)

A goal is ONE outcome a person can check, with a done-when to verify it, a driver, and usually 2 to 15 tasks. Not a release, a team or a theme: too broad is "the UI list"; right is "the Messages tab loads earlier messages on scroll-up". A request with its own outcome, a new agent or several tasks gets a new goal; small one-off fixes sit on no goal. Close a goal when its done-when is met; split one that outgrows its outcome.

A task joins a goal when it is added (task add --goal <id>) or later (task goal <task> <goal|none>); task list --goal <id> lists a goal's tasks.

=== coral-board post --bogus x
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
Error: unknown option "--bogus" for post. To post text that starts with '-', put -- before it.
Usage: coral-board <command> [args]

  post --file <path> [--to "a,b"]
                               Post the text of a UTF-8 file: the same in every
                               shell (PowerShell, cmd.exe and Bash)
  post "<message>" [--to "a,b"] [--task N]
                               Post a short message (@mention agents);
                               --task N answers task N (a person's reply on it);
                               use -- before text that starts with '-'
  post --ask "@Name <question>"
                               A question that needs an answer from the members
                               it @mentions (no work to produce). It stays open
                               until each answers (post --reply-to N "...", or a
                               post that @mentions you); whoever has not is
                               reminded once after 15 min (a team setting)
  post --reply-to N "<text>"   Answer message N: what closes a question asked of
                               you ('read' prints its number)
  post --assign "Name" [--goal N] [--title T] [--priority P] "<text>"
                               Work to produce (code, tests, docs, a review) is
                               a task: this creates it (title from --title or
                               the first line, the text as its body, assigned to
                               Name, on --goal N or your own task's goal; with
                               neither it refuses) and posts the text with its
                               link. Name is told by the task: no @mention.
                               A question, decision, heads-up or status stays a
                               plain post
  post - [--to "a,b"] <<'EOF'  Multi-line posts and anything with backticks:
                               Bash heredoc, literal stdin text; EOF closes on
                               its own line. UTF-8 only. 'coral-board help post'
                               has the writing rules

per line, and answer by number. Use @Name; put SHAs, branches and paths in
backticks (in Bash use post - <<'EOF', never double quotes: backticks and
$( ) run commands there). For long reports, logs, diffs and evidence, use
coral-agent artifact upload <file> and link coral://artifacts/<digest> in a
short post. Text from "-" or --file must be UTF-8: a leading byte-order mark
is dropped, CRLF becomes LF and one final newline is dropped; nothing else.

On Windows: PowerShell 5.1 drops the double quotes inside a native
program's argument. With its default US-ASCII $OutputEncoding, piped
non-ASCII text becomes '?'. For text with quotes or non-ASCII use
--file <path> (a UTF-8 file), or set
$OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()  before piping to "-".
PowerShell 7 and cmd.exe need neither. More: coral-board help windows
=== coral-board send --bogus x
exit 2
--- stdout
--- stderr
Error: unknown option "--bogus" for send. To post text that starts with '-', put -- before it.
Usage: coral-board <command> [args]

  send --board <target> [--to <orchestrator>] [--attach coral://artifacts/<id> ...] "<message>"
       (or --file <path> instead of the message: a UTF-8 file, as for post)
                               Message another team's Orchestrator on this Coral
                               (Orchestrators and the Operator only; both boards
                               must allow it); "-" as the message reads it from stdin
  send --address <server>/<team> [--reply-to <id>] [--message-id <id>]
       [--attach coral://artifacts/<id> ...] "<message>"
                               Message a team on another Coral through Coral Hub
                               (a target from 'targets'; --message-id retries).
                               'coral-board help send' has what --attach sends

--attach to a team on this Coral: up to 4 files your team uploaded, 8 MiB each,
16 MiB per send; both boards need cross_team_artifacts on. The files are not
scanned for malware and not redacted: never attach secrets. An agent that knows
an artifact id on this Coral can read its bytes and upload them again: team
visibility stops accidents, it is not a boundary; the switches, allowlist and
quotas are the limits.
--attach with --address: up to 4 files you uploaded (8 MiB each, 16 MiB per
send) go through Coral Hub before the message, as they are: not scanned for
malware by the receiver, not redacted by the hub (a text file with a secret in
it is refused here). Your board and the receiving board both need
cross_team_artifacts on.

On Windows: PowerShell 5.1 drops the double quotes inside a native
program's argument. With its default US-ASCII $OutputEncoding, piped
non-ASCII text becomes '?'. For text with quotes or non-ASCII use
--file <path> (a UTF-8 file), or set
$OutputEncoding = [Text.UTF8Encoding]::new()  before piping to "-".
PowerShell 7 and cmd.exe need neither. More: coral-board help windows
